Requests game graphics adjustments on the PC for the selected resolution and FPS, when supported by the host. Takes effect on the next stream.
Helps video recovery after lost or corrupted packets by invalidating unusable reference frames.
On: automatically detects local or remote connections from the host address. Off: forces local LAN mode. Takes effect on the next stream.
Waits for the Vita display VBlank when presenting video frames. This can reduce tearing, but may affect latency and frame pacing.
Limits presentation to the selected FPS by dropping excess decoded frames when they arrive too quickly.
Requests audio playback through the PC's speakers or headphones when supported by the host. Takes effect on the next stream.

Video: resolution, codec, target FPS and video payload bitrate (Mbps). FPS: received, decoded and submitted to PAF; PAF is not the physical display rate. RTT/variation: round-trip network delay and its fluctuation (ms). Drops: frames missing before decoding, skipped by the pacer or replaced in the PAF queue (%). Decode call/PAF queue: average decoder call time and queue wait (ms). Host min/max/avg: PC processing time (ms), when available. Video stalled: no recent frames. Unavailable measurements are hidden.
On: fills the Vita screen and crops edges when the aspect ratios differ. Off: fits the entire image.
Enables diagnostic messages in psp2shell. No log file is written.
Sends the Vita gyroscope and accelerometer data to the PC as motion input.
Swaps the functions of R1/L1 with R2/L2.
Sets the two-finger scroll speed in Mouse Absolute mode. Higher multipliers scroll faster; cursor speed is unchanged.
Captures the Vita PS button during streaming. A single press is sent to the PC as a PS/Xbox button; a double press stops the stream. Hold to open Vita Quick Actions.
Only active when Touchscreen mode is Off. Top left: keyboard; top right: stop stream (also works without PS button capture); bottom left: L3; bottom right: R3.
Selects how the Vita front touchscreen is presented to the host: off, DS4-style touchpad, absolute mouse, or Sunshine tablet mode.
Loads Cross, Circle, Square and Triangle mappings from ux0:data/moonlight/vita.conf. Overrides the X/O swap setting. Takes effect on the next stream.
Reserves a margin along this back-touchscreen edge, in pixels of the virtual 960x544 touch area. Higher values move the active area inward.

USER GUIDE
Swipe to turn pages · Double-tap to zoom
PC games on your Vita
Video, audio and controls
Play PC games or use the desktop through Sunshine. Moonlight sends Vita controls back to your PC.
Prepare Sunshine
Install Sunshine on the PC. Finish capture, audio and gamepad setup; add your games in Applications.
Use the same home network
Allow Sunshine through the PC firewall. Guest Wi-Fi or client isolation can prevent PCs from appearing.
Games run on the PC. Moonlight receives H.264 video and stereo audio. The PC must stay on.
Connect and pair
Select your PC
Open Moonlight. PCs appear automatically while the main screen is idle. Select the PC you want to use.
Add an address if needed
Tap the PC-plus icon at the top left. Enter a hostname or IPv4 address, optionally followed by :47989.
Enter the Vita PIN on the PC
Keep the PIN screen open. In Sunshine on the PC, select PIN, enter the Vita number and confirm.
The PC web UI is usually https://localhost:47990. On Vita, enter the PC address, not that web-UI URL.
Manage saved PCs
Pairing saves the PC
A new PC is saved after successful pairing. Cancelling the PIN or a failed attempt leaves it temporary.
Delete through the corner menu
Open the bottom-right menu > Delete. Select PCs, then Delete > OK. Cancel in the confirmation keeps selection.
Understand the status indicator
The dot on a saved PC checks reachability. It does not guarantee pairing or that streaming is ready.
Delete removes the local record and server pin. To revoke the Vita on the PC, remove it in Sunshine too.
Apps and LiveArea
Start a game or the desktop
Select a paired PC, wait for its application list, then select an app. Use Back to return to your PCs.
Switch a running host app
If another app is running on the PC, Moonlight asks to quit it. Yes switches apps; No keeps it running.
Launch from LiveArea
After loading Apps, LiveArea shows the last PC and up to six apps. Tap the PC card or an app shortcut.
LiveArea shows the last successful list. It does not refresh PCs or apps in the background after Moonlight closes.
Gamepad controls
Front buttons and sticks
The sticks, directional pad, face buttons, L/R, Start and Select act as the PC gamepad controls.
Rear panel: upper half
By default, touch the upper-left rear area for L2 and the upper-right rear area for R2.
Rear panel: lower half
Touch the lower-left rear area for L3 and the lower-right rear area for R3 (stick clicks).
Input settings can swap L1/R1 with L2/R2. Advanced settings can add margins to the rear touch areas.
PS button and stopping
Double-press PS to stop
With PS button capture enabled, press PS twice quickly to stop streaming and return to the app list.
Single press and hold
A short single press sends the home button to the PC. Hold PS for the Vita Quick Actions menu.
Stopping keeps the PC app open
An ordinary stream stop does not quit the PC game. Select the app again to reconnect or resume.
Without PS capture: enable touchscreen special keys with Touchscreen mode Off. Tap the top-right corner to stop.
Touch and keyboard
Choose a touchscreen mode
Input settings offer Off, DS4 touchpad, absolute mouse and Sunshine tablet. Host support varies by mode.
Use the corner shortcuts
With special keys enabled and touchscreen mode Off: top left opens the keyboard; top right stops streaming.
Switch keyboard languages
Enable languages in Vita Settings > Language > Input Languages. Switch on the native stream keyboard.
Special keys also map the bottom-left and bottom-right corners to L3/R3. PC address entry keeps its URL keyboard.
Picture and sound
Start with the defaults
Open the corner menu > Settings > Stream. Fresh defaults are 1280x720, 60 FPS and 5 Mbps.
Balance quality and smoothness
Higher resolution and bitrate need more bandwidth and decoding work. Reduce FPS or bitrate if playback stutters.
Fit the image or fill the screen
System > Fill screen crops the edges when shapes differ. Turn it off to see the complete image.
Stream > Play audio on PC also keeps sound on the host. Stop and restart the stream after changing settings.
Personalize input
Motion input
Enable motion sensors in Input to send Vita gyro and accelerometer data. The host and game must support them.
Controller identity and light
Choose the host controller type. The optional DS4/DualSense-style light overlay displays host RGB feedback.
Face-button mapping
Advanced > Use custom face-button mapping reads ux0:data/moonlight/vita.conf. Example: cross=b sends B from Cross.
Keys: cross/circle/square/triangle. Values: a/b/x/y. One key=value per line, without spaces; overrides X/O swap.
Connection help
PC not found
Check Sunshine, the PC LAN address, Wi-Fi isolation and firewall. Try manual IPv4 entry on the Vita.
PIN rejected or pairing busy
Read the error. Finish or cancel the old PIN attempt before retrying; Sunshine may still have a pending attempt.
Server certificate changed
Confirm the change on your PC. If expected, delete that saved PC locally, add it again and pair again.
Do not disable certificate checks. Cancelling or failing a new pairing attempt does not create a saved PC.
Playback and diagnostics
Video stutters or stops
Try lower FPS, bitrate or resolution. Check PC capture and network quality; an FPS setting is not a speed guarantee.
Input or touch does not work
Check Sunshine gamepad support and the selected Input mode. Corner shortcuts require touchscreen mode Off.
Show statistics or collect logs
System settings offer stream statistics and Debug log. Logs go to the psp2shell console, not a file.
For a report, include app version, Vita firmware, Sunshine version and stream settings. Keep pairing files private.
Updates and saved data
Install the complete package
Close Moonlight, then install the full system VPK with VitaShell. Allow UNSAFE homebrew in your Vita setup.
Back up before an update
Keep a private copy of the whole ux0:data/moonlight/ folder. It holds your pairing identity, PCs and server pins.
Keep track of your Settings
AppSettings stores preferences separately from the PC folder. Note them before reinstalling or switching profiles.
Settings > About shows build information. Licenses and credits lists the components. The manual is available offline.
